authority: The policy `tests/architecture/reachable-controls.test.ts` reads. Editing this file changes what the guard enforces; editing the test changes how it enforces it. Keep the two apart so an exemption is reviewable as data.
class: a control that gates production behaviour, whose ENABLING call exists only in tests — so the gated path is dark in the shipped composition while the code reads as if it ships

history.first: `configureWorkflowMaterializer` — set `moduleViewMaterializer`, which gated the ES v2 read path in `handleGet` and the state-snapshot refresh in `handleSet`. Called from four test files and from nothing in `src/`, so `workflow get` always took the legacy state-file path and `get --asOf` silently answered with tip state instead of a bounded fold.
history.why-invisible: Nothing was red. The gated branches had tests, because the tests called the enabler themselves — which is exactly what made the coverage look complete while the shipped path was unreachable. It surfaced only when a regression test for a fix inside one of those branches passed with the fix removed.

rule.statement: A function whose name marks it as an enabler — it configures, registers, installs, enables or wires something a production path then checks — must have at least one caller under `src/`. A caller under `tests/` does not count, because a test that enables a path is testing a composition the product does not ship.
rule.why-name-based: The signal is intent, and intent lives in the name. A structural check cannot tell 'sets a value some branch reads' from 'sets a value nothing reads' without whole-program dataflow; the naming convention is what makes the population decidable, and it is the convention this repository already follows.

enablerNamePatterns.why: sets a module-level or container-level value a consumer later reads
adds an implementation to a registry a dispatcher resolves from
attaches a hook, handler or middleware to a live surface
flips a capability a guarded branch tests
connects a component to the composition root

allowlist.why: Not an enabler. It is a PREDICATE over an install manifest — `installManifest` + `VouchesForDir`, returning a boolean — and matches `^install[A-Z]` by prefix coincidence alone. Nothing is gated on calling it, so there is no dark path behind it. Encoding 'is a predicate' into the name rule is harder than recording the one case, and a rule that tried would start producing false negatives.

A GENUINE instance, exempted only to keep it visible while it is triaged rather than to excuse it. It copies the bundled MCP server into `~/.claude/mcp-servers/` so the runtime can launch it, and no install path calls it — only its own test. Either the installer lost that step or the step was superseded; deciding which needs the install surface's owner, and guessing wrong breaks installs. Not fixed here because this change is scoped to the workflow materializer.

allowlistSchema.why: the reason a production caller is genuinely not owed — not 'we will wire it later'
allowlistSchema.expiry: YYYY-MM-DD after which the guard fails on this entry

killFixture.why: `configureWorkflowMaterializer` as it stood before it was removed, verbatim. The guard must report it. A guard with no failing subject has no evidence that it works.

sourceExtensionsWhy: This tree contains AUTHORED `.js` under `src/` (the lifecycle bridges), not just compiled output — and compiled output is gitignored, so a tracked-file walk cannot pick it up by accident. Scanning `.ts` alone reported `installSkills` as dark while `src/lifecycle/install-skills-bridge.js` imports and calls it.

oracleRoster.class: an ORACLE — a method that walks durable state and returns a verdict — that exists only for its own tests, so the property it checks is enforced nowhere in the shipped composition. The name rule above cannot see it: an oracle is not named as an enabler, and it is usually a class method rather than an exported function, which the enabler extractor does not read.
oracleRoster.history: `EventStore.runBundleIntegrityCheck` shipped with the run-bundle store and had no caller under `src/` for a week: every executed intent was a settled stream with no reference, and nothing an operator could run would have said so. The doctor check `run-bundle-integrity` became its caller; this roster is what keeps it one.
oracleRoster.rule: Each rostered oracle declares its CALL CHAIN from the method that holds the verdict to the roster the composition root iterates. Every hop must reference the previous hop's symbol in its executable source (imports and re-exports stripped, comments and strings masked). A chain is only as reachable as its weakest hop: a probe forwarder wired to nothing is the same defect one level up, so a one-hop reference scan is not enough.

chain.why: the probe bundle forwards the store method
the roster the composer iterates names the check

killFixture.why: the probe factory as it stood while the oracle was dormant, verbatim. Run as hop 1 of the chain above it must be reported as broken — a scanner that passes it has gone blind to the defect this roster exists for.

shippedDefaultTwins.class: a test context that turns a shipped default off, so its cases prove a composition that the product does not ship while no case proves the shipped one
shippedDefaultTwins.history: The replay cases of settle said that a replay leaves the tail of the stream where it was. Every case ran with telemetry off. Under the shipped default the dispatcher appends a telemetry gate row for each call, so the statement was false in the shipped composition, and no case showed it. The levelling cases of settle also kept the state document in a JSON file, and the shipped store keeps it in the `workflow_state` row.
shippedDefaultTwins.rule: Each acceptance or settle test file that turns a shipped default off has a twin case that keeps the default, or a reason recorded here with an owner. A twin names its file, its case and a literal that the body of the case holds to keep the default. A record for a file that no longer turns the default off is stale and fails the guard.

defaults.shipped: `initializeContext` sets `enableTelemetry` unless EXARCHOS_TELEMETRY is `false`, so the dispatcher wraps each call in the telemetry wrapper
the composition root configures the SQLite backend, so the state document is the `workflow_state` row and not a `.state.json` file

No twin runs the admitted calls with the default, and the wrapper then appends an emissions gate row to the subject stream. Not a settle context. The twin is owed, and this record keeps the gap visible.

contextSchema.file: repo-relative path of the test file that turns the default off
contextSchema.default: the id of the shipped default
contextSchema.twin: a case that keeps the default: its file, its name, and a literal that its body holds
contextSchema.reason: why the file needs no twin, or the gap that stays open, when there is no twin
contextSchema.owner: who accepts the record of a reason

killFixture.why: The first record names a twin and the second records a reason. A policy without either record must leave its context unaccounted for. A checker that passes it has gone blind to the defect this rule exists for.
